I'm so sorry for the loss of your mom. Grief is deeply personal, and there's no right or wrong way to move through it. It's okay to feel a wide range of emotions — sadness, anger, confusion, even moments of peace — sometimes all in the same day. Be gentle with yourself and allow yourself to feel whatever comes up without judgment.

Some people find comfort in talking about their loved one, creating rituals or keepsakes, or connecting with others who understand loss. Supporting yourself with basics like rest, nourishment, and movement can also help, even when it feels hard. If you're struggling to cope or feeling overwhelmed, reaching out to a grief counselor or a support group can make a real difference. You don't have to carry this alone. If you ever feel like you're in crisis or having thoughts of harming yourself, please reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust right away. Your feelings matter, and support is available.
